title: [Running Wylder] Katie Douglas
desc: Building a store that happens to sell running stuff: turning nearly twenty years in fashion into a point of view on product, opening a store in San Francisco after a layoff sped up the plan, skipping gait analysis, using merch and a Substack to build the brand, and protecting the community that makes it work by choosing to stay small instead of scaling.

title: Shelf Stable: What happened to Jones Soda?
desc: Tracing the rise, decline, and reinvention of Jones Soda: building a cult following through fan-submitted labels and unconventional distribution, spending millions to break into supermarkets, struggling with the economics of shelf space and retail expansion, and finding new growth through licensed products like Fallout.

title: [Pangram] Max Spero
desc: Building an AI writing detection company: training a model on matched human and AI text, moving from content moderation sales to a self-serve product for teachers, working through long school sales cycles, and managing false positives and training costs as the models scale.

title: [Primis Imports] Damian Primis
desc: Building an imported olive oil and Mediterranean pantry brand: planning around one harvest a year, shipping and warehousing heavy glass, pricing from full-container cost, balancing direct sales, wholesale, and retail, and absorbing tariffs and fuel costs as the line grows.

title: [Miracle Mama] Whitney Rowell
desc: Building a functional cookie brand for new mothers: turning a blog recipe into a business, finding a manufacturer that could bake fresh cookies, balancing direct sales, Amazon, and retail, working with hospitals and gifting, and expanding beyond lactation as the company takes on funding.

title: [Mikey's Pies] Mikey Deegan
desc: Building a frozen savory pie business in New York: using drops to match production to demand, working from a commercial kitchen, sourcing local ingredients, pricing for repeat purchase, and trading early flexibility for inventory, fulfillment, and production capacity as the business scales.

title: [TofuGo] Caroline Dai
desc: Building a shelf-stable savory tofu snack brand: finding scarce North American co-manufacturing for ambient tofu, designing vacuum-sealed packaging that works on shelf, converting early viral DTC demand into retail, and using aisle placement for consumer education.

title: [Matic Robots] Mehul Nariyawala
desc: Building a home robotics company around one of the most advanced robot vacuums on the market: seven years of product development, betting on camera-based computer vision, manufacturing domestically, iterating on pricing and recurring revenue, managing supply constraints, and designing a robot consumers can actually trust inside their homes.

title: [Yardsale] Cristina Ashbaugh
desc: Building an outdoor brand from magnetic ski poles to owned retail: solving a surprisingly difficult manufacturing problem, expanding into bags and apparel, navigating wholesale and Shark Tank, and turning a search for warehouse space into a coffee shop and retail store.

title: [Rite of Way] Alex Brands
desc: Building a luxury fragrance brand: validating the category before building, developing archetype-led scents with a perfumer through brief and mods, pricing into a luxury peer set, forecasting demand against MOQs, and using selective independent retail as trial, acquisition, and brand context for a product you have to smell.

title: [Great Circle Ventures] Jacob Afriat
desc: Examining how early-stage consumer investors decide which brands to back: sourcing and filtering deals, evaluating founders and unit economics, setting valuations, allocating follow-on capital, and determining what actually makes a business venture-backable.

title: [Springdale Ventures] Dan Graham & Mollye Santulli
desc: Examining how early-stage consumer investors decide which brands to back: sourcing and filtering deals, evaluating founders and unit economics, setting valuations, constructing a portfolio, allocating follow-on capital, and underwriting for venture-scale returns.

title: [Alexandra Spitz] New Mom School
desc: Building an in-person postpartum education business around cohort-based classes for new mothers: balancing class size and economics, acquiring customers through local referrals and community, standardizing curriculum and instructor quality, and scaling a high-touch experience through franchising.

title: [Joy Supply] Lindsay Leopold
desc: Building a better-for-you cookie brand around regenerative ingredients: adapting a family oat cookie recipe for commercial production, sourcing through a more custom supply chain, finding the right co-manufacturer, pricing and packaging for retail, and managing inventory, fulfillment, and distribution as the business grows.

title: [Caro] Caroline McKay
desc: Breaking down how a modern PR agency operates, including media pitching, client readiness, pricing, founder participation, affiliate commerce, lower-cost service models, team structure, and the challenge of scaling a high-touch firm.

title: [Noshi for Kids] Tomo Delaney
desc: Rebuilding a children's food brand around naturally colored frosting: lessons from Walmart and Shark Tank, a manufacturing breakdown, DTC-first distribution, TikTok Shop and Amazon, pricing, margins, and the tradeoffs of turning a novel product into something consumers already understand.

title: [Biche] Alexandra Pauly
desc: Building a prestige pet grooming brand: formulation, pet-friendly fragrance, pricing, customer education, retail positioning, DTC acquisition, fundraising, and disciplined SKU expansion.

title: [Brightland] Aishwarya Iyer
desc: Building a premium pantry brand around California-grown olive oil: product costs, DTC economics, pricing, inventory, gifting, collaborations, selective retail expansion, fundraising, and operating with a leaner team.

title: [MAHSA CHAI®] Mahsa Darabi
desc: Building a premium powdered chai company from a personal kitchen blend: sourcing twelve ingredients, working with tea and spice suppliers, moving from hand-filled tins to local production partners, pricing against concentrates and functional beverage alternatives, educating customers, expanding into cafes and retailers, and scaling without compromising quality.

title: [Betty Jo's] Erin Forden & Maddie Nehlen
desc: Scaling a pastry-inspired ice cream business in Brooklyn: handmade pints, monthly drops, customer pickup, repeat purchasing, collaborations, events, wholesale constraints, and the tradeoffs between local craft and growth.

title: [Terra Kaffe] Sahand Dilmaghani
desc: Building a connected coffee hardware company: contract manufacturing, product iteration, firmware updates, pricing ladders, coffee subscriptions, rentals, B2B demand, and the trade-offs of expanding beyond one premium machine.

title: [Jamie's Farm] Jamie Kim
desc: Building a premium granola brand around ghee, culinary flavors, and regional retail: sourcing differentiated ingredients, finding a co-packer that can handle dairy, managing cherry and vanilla supply constraints, financing inventory for Whole Foods growth, and scaling without defaulting to the venture-backed CPG playbook.

title: [Pistakio] Francine Voit & Nicola Buffo
desc: Building a pistachio spread brand around real pistachio flavor: sourcing California pistachios, teaching customers new use cases through demos and food service, balancing premium pricing with everyday usage, and scaling from local retail into broader West Coast distribution.

title: [RIP Cold Brew] Brendan Flannery
desc: Building a ready-to-drink cold brew brand around active, on-the-go coffee occasions: developing smooth shelf-stable canned coffee, testing retail environments, pricing DTC around trial and learning, and expanding into half-caf, latte, and flavored black coffee.

title: 9 Mini Interviews

title: [Honey Dept.] Noah Phillips
